The test image shows two tomato plant stems with roots attached, displaying brown/tan discoloration of the vascular/cortical tissue extending from roots upward. The fibrous roots are dead/brown. This pattern suggests a vascular or soilborne disease. Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

Let me view one reference from each candidate.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Two tomato plants uprooted, stems shown against white background
- Extensive brown/tan cortical decay extending from the root system up the lower stem
- Dead, brown fibrous roots
- Green upper stem transitioning to brown at the crown area
- The stems appear to be deliberately shown to reveal internal vascular/cortical discoloration

**Reference image comparisons:**
- Verticillium_Wilt reference (Bugwood_10): showed whole plant with leaf yellowing — different presentation but vascular browning is the classic diagnostic feature
- Southern_Blight (Bugwood_5): field-level wilting without the stem tissue detail
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (Bugwood_2): showed aerial wilting
- Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (Bugwood_7): surface stem cankers — somewhat similar dark stem lesions

**Reasoning:** The test image shows the classic diagnostic presentation of **Verticillium Wilt** — uprooted plants with the lower stem/crown area revealing extensive brown vascular/cortical discoloration extending from the dead root system upward. This is the standard way Verticillium wilt is diagnosed (cut or expose the lower stem to reveal brown vascular streaking). No white mycelium (ruling out Southern Blight/Sclerotinia), no surface cankers matching Alternaria.
